sections.h2: Where is the Ross County Recorder and how do I reach the office?
sections.html:
The Ross County Recorder works from the courthouse at 2 North Paint Street, Suite E, Chillicothe, Ohio 45601, and answers at 740-702-3000. Documents sent by mail go to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, and the office email is rossrec@bright.net. Courthouse neighbors include the treasurer in Suite F, which makes it easy to settle a tax balance and record a deed in one trip.

The county has a long paper trail. Ross County was formed on August 20, 1798 as the sixth county of the Northwest Territory, and Chillicothe was Ohio's first and third capital. Nineteenth-century surveyors described almost one hundred earthwork enclosures and five hundred mounds in the county, and Hopewell Culture National Historical Park and Adena State Memorial are among its protected sites. Modern deeds sit on top of more than two centuries of recorded transfers.

sections.h2: What does the Ross County Recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's fee sheet, effective January 1, 2025, prices a document by page count. One or two pages cost $39.00, three pages cost $47.00, and each added page costs $8.00 more. Non-standard documents under section 317.114 of the Revised Code take an extra $20.00, and each marginal reference takes $4.00. The office states that its recording fees are set by the Ohio Legislature.

Source: Ross County Recorder Table of Fees. The schedule continues to 88 pages at $727.00 and then adds $8.00 for each page beyond that.

State law explains the structure. Section 317.32 sets a base fee and a matching housing trust fund fee for each page, and lets a county add a document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars. A postage-paid, self-addressed envelope is required with every filing, so include one when you mail a deed.

sections.h2: What other recorder charges should a Ross County seller know about?
sections.html:
• Certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.
  • Plain copies cost $2.00 per printed page, so a two-page document is $7 and a three-page document is $9.
  • Faxes cost $2.00 per page to a local or toll-free number and $4.00 per page to a toll number.
  • The recorder's page says an original recorded deed is not needed to sell or borrow against a property, since a certified copy from the office is as good as the original.

These are the office's own figures, and they apply to documents the office handles after a sale, such as copying a recorded deed for a title company or an heir.

sections.h2: How do I search Ross County records online, and what should I avoid?
sections.html:
The recorder's website says most records go back to January 1, 1974 and further, and can be viewed and downloaded free from home through the county's CountyFusion search. The office also assists people in person while they wait. Anyone can see a deed, mortgage or release this way before listing a house.

The office warns about private companies that mail letters or turn up in online searches charging $79.99 to $99.99 for copies of a deed. These companies are not government offices, and the same records are free to view at the courthouse offices. The recorder calls those offers a scam for money, and recommends skipping them. One exception applies to military discharge papers: a DD214 is not a full public record, and only the veteran, a veterans' service office or a funeral director handling burial services can get an unredacted certified copy, free of charge.

sections.h2: What must happen before a Ross County deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
The deed must be signed and acknowledged. Section 5301.01 of the Revised Code lists who can take the acknowledgment: a judge, a clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor. Next comes the Ross County Auditor, who endorses the deed after the buyer files a statement of value under section 319.202. That statement answers whether the seller's taxes were reduced by programs such as homestead, and whether the land was in the farm valuation program, which can carry a recoupment charge.

The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax to the auditor before the deed is presented. Under section 322.02, a county may set that transfer tax at up to thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. The Ross County Auditor can tell you the figure that applies.

sections.h2: How does Ross County property tax fit into a deed closing?
sections.html:
Ross County collects real estate tax one year behind. The treasurer's FAQ explains that taxes attach to the property, not the owner, so a buyer can receive a bill right after a purchase and normally gets a credit for the prorated share in the closing papers. The first-half 2026 bills were due February 20 and the second half August 21, and the treasurer can give the 2027 dates. Ask for a written balance before closing and bring it to the title company.

If back taxes are owed, the treasurer's Delinquent Tax Contract splits them into five equal installments, and the SMART Payments Program spreads them over 30 months or longer. A seller with a contract open should confirm what balance stays with the property. The treasurer's penalty rules are 5% for payments received within ten days after the due date and 10% after that.

sections.h2: What if an old family deed in Ross County lacks two witnesses?
sections.html: Ohio treats most such deeds as valid. For an instrument signed before February 1, 2002 and never witnessed by two people as the earlier statute asked, section 5301.01(B) presumes it properly executed unless fraud produced the signature. Once the deed is on file with the county recorder, later buyers and lenders are charged with notice of it. Heirs in Ross County who find a mid-century deed in a drawer should still check that it was actually recorded, because the index at the recorder's office is what a title company searches.

sections.h2: What does the Ross County housing stock look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 76,429 residents and 32,165 housing units, with owners living in 69.6% of homes. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $171,500, median monthly owner costs are $1,304 with a mortgage and $487 without, and 59 building permits were issued in 2025. About 87.9% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Ross County includes the city of Chillicothe, the villages of Adelphi, Bainbridge, Clarksburg, Frankfort, Kingston and South Salem, and 16 townships. Ohio University has run a campus in Chillicothe since 1966. The terrain is frequent wooded hills with farmland between them, so any sale of acreage should be checked with the auditor for farm valuation before the deed is signed.

faqs.q: How much does the Ross County Recorder charge for a one or two page deed?
faqs.a: $39.00 on the fee sheet effective January 1, 2025. Each added page after the second costs $8.00 more, and a non-standard document adds $20.00.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a deed to the Ross County Recorder?
faqs.a: Mail it to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, with the fee and a postage-paid, self-addressed envelope, which the office requires with every filing. The street address is 2 North Paint Street, Suite E.

faqs.q: Can I get Ross County records without paying a service?
faqs.a: Yes. Most records back to January 1, 1974 can be viewed and downloaded free through the county's CountyFusion site. Copies made in the office are $2.00 per printed page on the fee sheet.

faqs.q: Do I need the original deed to sell my Ross County house?
faqs.a: No. The recorder says an original deed is not needed to sell or get a mortgage, and a certified copy from the office is as good as the original. Certified copies are $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

faqs.q: Who endorses a Ross County deed before it is recorded?
faqs.a: The County Auditor, after the buyer files the statement of value under section 319.202. The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax to the auditor first.
